title: Incomplete Passive Indicative
subtitle: Present, imperfect and future (incomplete aspect): all four conjugations plus 3rd -iō
intro:
The passive uses the same stems and time markers as the active. Only the personal endings change: -r, -ris, -tur, -mur, -minī, -ntur replace -ō/-m, -s, -t, -mus, -tis, -nt. Where the active ends in -ō, the passive adds -r (amō → amor, amābō → amābor). Where it ends in -m, the -m is replaced (amābam → amābar, mittam → mittar).

Watch the 2nd person singular:

  • A short e appears before -ris in the 3rd-conjugation present (mitteris, caperis) and the -bi- future (amāberis, vidēberis).
  • mitteris (present, “you are sent”) and mittēris (future, “you will be sent”) differ only in vowel length.
  • -ris has an alternate ending -re (amāre, amābāre, amābere). It's not drilled here.
